transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I came in because... well, I keep hearing people talking about me. It usually happens when I'm at work. I'll hear voices coming through the conference room walls, or even from my phone when it's completely turned off. It's usually the board members or my staff, and they're saying things like I'm ruining the company. It sounds so incredibly clear that I've actually answered them out loud before I even realize that no one else in the room heard a thing.
Do you believe these people are actually trying to harm you or sabotage you?

I... I don't know if I would say they're trying to actually harm me, or actively sabotage me. I'm really not sure about that. I haven't noticed any kind of plot or anything. I just know what I hear them saying—that I'm doing a terrible job and ruining the company. But as far as them actually trying to hurt me or take me down... I don't know, I just haven't seen anything like that, I just hear the talking.
Have you had a period where you felt unusually high, energized, or euphoric for days at a time?

No, I haven't. I don't think I've ever felt euphoric or... unusually energized for days at a time. Honestly, I'm usually just exhausted from dealing with work and hearing them talk about me all day. So, no, nothing like that.
Have you used any drugs or substances around the times when you hear these voices?
No, I don't use drugs. I mean, I drink coffee, but no illegal substances or anything like that. I don't even really drink alcohol. It's just... the voices are there anyway.
How long have you been hearing these voices?
It's been about three months now. Yeah, for the past three months I've been hearing them talking about me, either coming through the walls or sometimes from my phone.
Have you had any recent medical illness or head injury?
No, I haven't. Um, I haven't been sick lately, and I definitely haven't hit my head or anything like that. Physically, I've been completely fine.
Have you found yourself becoming much less interested in being around other people than you used to be?

Yes, definitely. It's... a big change. I used to be the person driving every idea, always calling people after openings. But now, I can just sit at my desk for hours staring at the agenda. I barely speak to my staff anymore, or even my husband. I just feel almost nothing about the work I used to love.
Have other people told you that your speech has been hard to follow or that your thoughts seem jumbled?

No, no one has said anything like that. I mean... like I just mentioned, I really don't talk to people much right now anyway, so there isn't much opportunity for them to notice. But when I do have to say something, I think I make sense. No one has told me otherwise.
Have these problems made it hard for you to keep up with your work responsibilities the way you used to?

Yes, it really has. I'm... I'm just no longer reliably able to run the division. I can't seem to keep up with basic executive decisions anymore. My senior staff have quietly taken over a lot of the work I used to handle myself. And it's happening at home, too. My husband has had to manage most of the household responsibilities because I just... I leave things unfinished, or I don't even start them at all.
Have you been neglecting basic self-care, like bathing or changing clothes, more than usual?

No, I don't think so. I mean... I still shower and get dressed every day. I might not put as much effort into my appearance as I used to for work, but I'm still keeping up with the basics. My husband hasn't said anything about that, at least.
Did these experiences begin very suddenly?

No, it wasn't sudden at all. It's... it's been building up for a while now. I'd say about two years and four months. That's when the company expanded and they put me in charge of the new arts-and-commerce division. Everything just started slowly unraveling after that.
